extracted_details.description_text: The supplied INF identifies Surface Integration Driver version 120.8.4.0, dated 05/06/2026, for the ACPI hardware ID ACPI\MSHW0530 on x64 Windows 10 build 19041 or later. INFDescriptionData was semantically analyzed: it installs a demand-start kernel driver, references three Surface power-policy provisioning packages, enables the platform's KIP-supported setting, configures display backlight energy-estimation data, hides the estimated remaining battery discharge time, enables screen refresh on a long power-button press, and adjusts fvevol request limits with an INF comment noting BitLocker SSD-performance intent. No exact-version, previous-version, latest-version, or family release notes were retrieved, so the enrichment is based on the exact version declared in the provided INF rather than vendor release-note claims. The supplied Intel portal links concern Intel Management Engine/chipset downloads and do not identify this Surface package; no Surface download or release-notes URL could be verified. The INF contains driver and provisioning-policy files, not firmware payloads, so firmware_flag is false.
key_components: SurfaceIntegrationDriver.sys: kernel driver associated with ACPI\MSHW0530; configured as demand-start.

Three policy packages are copied to the Driver Store and registered through device properties: Surface.Power.Policy.Defaults.ppkg, Surface.Power.Policy.WIN10.Defaults.ppkg, and Surface.Power.Policy.WIN11-0.Defaults.ppkg.
SurfaceService registry capability PlatformKipSupported is set to 1; the INF comment explicitly connects this setting to KIP power-saving features.
The display energy-estimation configuration supplies a 14-point backlight brightness/power curve and sets display-panel power-estimation factors to zero.
Windows power configuration hides the estimated battery discharge time and enables screen refresh following a long power-button press.

BitLocker fvevol configuration sets maximum encrypt, decrypt, and per-I/O crypto request values to 0x40; the INF comment says the encrypt-request limit is intended to improve SSD performance under BitLocker.
key_functionalities: Installs and registers the Surface Integration kernel driver for the INF-declared ACPI hardware ID.
Provides default and OS-specific Surface power-policy provisioning packages for Windows 10 and Windows 11.
Marks KIP as supported on the platform to enable its power-saving features.
Configures brightness-dependent backlight power data for Windows display energy estimation.
Suppresses the user-visible estimated battery discharge-time value.
Enables screen refresh on a long press of the power button.
Raises the configured fvevol encrypt/decrypt/crypto request limits to 64; the stated SSD-performance rationale is specifically present in the INF comment.
extracted_details.major_components_functionalities_descrip: This enrichment uses the exact version 120.8.4.0 and date in the supplied INF; no version-specific or family release notes were retrieved. Semantic analysis of INFDescriptionData shows that the package installs a demand-start Surface kernel driver for ACPI\MSHW0530 and registers default, Windows 10, and Windows 11 power-policy packages. It explicitly enables the platform KIP capability, whose INF comment associates it with KIP power-saving features, and supplies a 14-point display backlight power curve for energy estimation. Other INF settings hide estimated battery discharge time, enable screen refresh after a long power-button press, and set fvevol request limits to 64, with the INF commenting on BitLocker SSD-performance intent. These are INF-documented configuration behaviors, not claims about changes introduced by this version; the supplied Intel portal links do not establish a Surface release-note or download source.
impact_details: KIP power-saving behavior may be affected because the INF enables PlatformKipSupported for SurfaceService.
Windows display energy estimation may be affected by the 14-point backlight power curve and display-panel estimation settings.
Battery UI behavior is affected because the INF configures Windows to hide the estimated remaining discharge time.
Long-press power-button behavior may include a screen refresh because the corresponding power setting is enabled.
BitLocker encrypted-storage throughput may be affected by the fvevol request limits; the INF itself states that the encrypt-request limit is intended to improve SSD performance under BitLocker.
Surface power-policy provisioning may be affected through the included default and OS-specific PPKG files.
